newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia PM tells West to stay out of ASEAN affairs.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia PM tells West to stay out of ASEAN affairs.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad told Western powers on Thursday to keep out of ASEAN affairs and said Southeast Asian nations must solve their own problems.

In an address opening the 30th anniversary meeting of foreign ministers of the Association of South East Asian Nations, he also bitterly accused "rogue speculators" of orchestrating "a well-planned effort to undermine the economies of all the ASEAN countries by destabilising their currencies".
Mahathir rejected Western criticism of ASEAN for admitting Burma, which joined the group along with Laos on Wednesday.
ASEAN now comprises Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam, Brunei, Burma and Laos.
Western nations led by the United States had criticised Burma's proposed membership because of its political and human rights record. Washington has imposed economic sanctions on Rangoon.
Mahathir said ASEAN membership would have a steadying influence on the domestic politics of member nations and help them progress.
"ASEAN must resist and reject such attempts at coercion. They are not a part of the ASEAN way," Mahathir said.
"We will resolve our problems in our own way and in our own time. No one, but no one, should assume that only they know the solutions to all problems.
"They have failed far too often for us to be convinced that only they know what is right and what is wrong," he said.
ASEAN prefers a policy of non-intervention in the affairs of other countries, opting for what it calls constructive engagement to bring about change and rejecting economic sanctions.

Mahathir made no specific mention, however, of the thorny problem of Cambodia, whose ASEAN membership was delayed after a coup by Second Prime Minister Hun Sen early this month plunged the country into turmoil.

Cambodian Foreign Minister Ung Huot, in an abrupt reversal of Phnom Penh's position, said on arrival in Kuala Lumpur on Tuesday that his country now was willing to accept ASEAN mediation to help resolve its problems.

Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas, who led an abortive mediation mission in mid-July accompanied by the foreign ministers of Thailand and the Philippines, said he had put fresh proposals to Ung Huot to help resolve the crisis.

"The three ministers will try to pick up the thread where we left it and continue our efforts," Alatas told Reuters on Thursday without going into specifics. "Now we have exchanged some views and now we are starting," he added.

Cambodia had been due to join ASEAN together with Burma and Laos on Wednesday, but ASEAN foreign ministers postponed its admission until they were assured of peace and stability in the war-racked nation.
A senior ASEAN source said Cambodia could possibly join at an annual ASEAN summit in December in Kuala Lumpur, or it may have to wait until after Cambodian elections due next May.
Mahathir stressed in his speech that the key to peace, stability and progress in the region depended on prosperity.
"Economic prosperity is really the answer to our security problems because with prosperity ASEAN will be taken seriously and its views respected," he said.
But he expressed concern over the "borderless world of the Information Age and the free market".
"We should know where we stand. We should know how we are going to handle the problems which will arise...

"Alone, none of the Southeast Asian countries will be able to protect itself. But nine Southeast Asian countries with half a billion people may be able to do something to help ourselves," Mahathir said.

Referring to recent speculative attacks on Southeast Asian currencies, he said He later told reporters that ASEAN should find ways to cooperate in defending its currencies, including more coordination among central banks in the region.
"Exactly how, I won't be able to say. But certainly by working together we can increase our clout and would be able to deal with this kind of problem which is common to all of us."

ASEAN sources said the two-day ministerial meeting was likely to discuss the group's relations with major political and economic groups such as the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum and the Asia Europe Meeting (ASEM).

The ministerial meeting will be followed by the ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF), which brings the group together with 11 other Asian and Western powers, including the United States, Japan, China, Russia and the European Union.
